absent: Selection rule between per-CPU and per-task recursion counter variants.
Exact bit values and full transition rules for queue and link state flags.
Watchdog sampling logic and timing that consumes the published activity stamp.
Structure layouts for devices, queues, packets, polling objects, and limiters.
Which configuration options gate each optional softnet_data member beyond the visible guards.
Lock ordering and interrupt expectations for queue start, stop, wake, and schedule paths.
Meaning and handling of drop versus consumed packet accounting reasons.
Full ioctl number layout beyond the type extraction shown.

findings.text: Per-CPU network bottom-half state aggregates receive polling membership plus queued work, completion chaining, generic output queue pointers, per-CPU transmit nesting counts, receive activity flags, processed and squeeze counters, RPS receive counts, backlog polling object, NUMA drop accounting, and deferred inter-processor state. Optional receive-steering, flow-limit, and transform-offload members exist only under their options.
Small page-pool guard pairs a pool reference with a bottom-half exclusion object, expressing that pool access is serialized against soft interrupt context.
Transmit recursion ceiling is the value eight. Helpers treat a nesting depth above that ceiling as excessive recursion.

Two alternative families expose transmit nesting depth. One family keeps the counter in per-CPU softnet transmit state; the other keeps it in per-task transmit state. Each family can read the current depth, test whether it exceeds the ceiling, increment it on entry, and decrement it on exit.

Transmit queue activation covers queue zero, every queue by iteration, or one indexed subqueue. Start clears the driver off mark, stop records activity time then sets that mark, wake clears it through the wake path, and schedule-all requests software-interrupt service for each queue.

Queue liveness is expressed with driver off, stack off, and frozen indications. Predicates report driver-stopped for one queue, device queue zero, an indexed subqueue, or the subqueue implied by a packet mapping, plus combined masks for any off and for off-or-frozen.

Byte queue limit accounting provides minimum-limit update, available-room query, cache prefetch for enqueue and completion paths, sent-side charging with stack-off handling, completion-side crediting with conditional rescheduling, and reset that clears stack-off and reinitializes the limiter. Device-level wrappers apply the queue-zero object; indexed helpers address one subqueue.
Without byte queue limit support the limiter helpers have no effect and availability reports neutral zero, so drivers without that option never observe stack backpressure from these paths.

Sent and stop paths publish an activity timestamp with ordered writes before setting an off mark, paired with watchdog-side reads and barriers; the sent path rechecks room after setting stack-off because another CPU may have freed space, and completion uses a full barrier before testing room so a wakeup cannot be lost and the queue wedged stopped.
Queue-index capping warns at a rate-limited level when the caller selects beyond the realized transmit queue count and then folds the selection to queue zero rather than using the invalid index.

CPU attribute mask helpers test one position with range warning, test online membership with null mask meaning position within range, and iterate to the next selected position with negative one accepted as start. The two-mask iterator tolerates either mask being absent by falling back to the present mask or simple succession.
Transmit packet steering configuration entry points are inert in these fragments and always report success without changing state.

Device link predicates report running from the start mark, carrier from absence of the no-carrier mark, presence from the present mark, dormant and testing from their marks, operational up from a snapshot equal to up or unknown for compatibility, and multiqueue from a transmit queue count above one.
Dormant and testing marks change only on edge: setting an already-set mark or clearing an already-clear mark does nothing, while a real transition emits a linkwatch event.

Packet-tap activity is sampled under a read-side critical section that is always released. Process and pool paths use local bottom-half locks. Inter-CPU receive-steering state separates owner-written head from cross-CPU readable fields with cacheline grouping and padding so tail, queued packets, and backlog state share intended lines.

Reference helpers tolerate a null device pointer by doing nothing. Otherwise they adjust either a per-CPU count or a shared count, couple counting with optional tracker allocation and release, and provide replace semantics that release the old reference, acquire the new one, and move tracker bookkeeping.
Reference-tracker allocation and release helpers in these fragments are inert and report success, so tracking only has effect when an external implementation is selected.

Interrupt-context packet release distinguishes a generic drop reason from a consumed reason, and any-context consume maps to the consumed reason. Receive aggregation delegates to the per-poll-object aggregation state, and fragment cleanup frees any cached incomplete packet then clears the cached pointer.

Forwardability requires the egress interface to be up. When length checking is enabled the packet must fit within the device limit plus framing allowances, unless segmentation offload is present. The forwarding helper first neutralizes zero-copy fragments, drops with a dropped counter on failure, otherwise scrubs identity across namespaces and clears priority.

Zero-copy detection reads shared packet descriptor flags; orphaning is skipped for non-zero-copy packets and for packets marked do-not-orphan, otherwise a copy of userspace-backed fragments is attempted and its failure forces a drop in the forwarding path.
Socket ioctl classification extracts the embedded type selector from the command number and compares it with the socket ioctl type value.
Message-level classes are an ordered set of bit positions terminated by a count sentinel, with an external name table expected to stay aligned when positions are added.
